title: embeddings-rerank-debug-scratchpad
content:
Context:
Small personal scratchpad while I triage the rerank+embeddings endpoint anomalies. This is messy notes-to-self: commands tried, raw snippets, timelines, quick hypotheses.

Summary of issue observed:
- Starting 2025-09-20 ~10:30 UTC we saw intermittent 500s from /v1/embeddings and downstream rerank timeouts.
- Two classes of symptoms: (A) dimension mismatch errors surfaced in the reranker: ValueError about vector shape; (B) latency spikes ~3–8s for otherwise <200ms requests.
- Affects customers using the hosted embeddings -> rerank pipeline that pins model to "open-embed-768" variant.

Quick timeline (rough):
- 2025-09-20 10:28 UTC: first error spike from synthetic probe (alerts).
- 2025-09-20 10:32–10:45 UTC: repeated 500s; many are dimension mismatch.
- 2025-09-20 11:10 UTC: roll-back to previous routing policy for a subset of traffic -> partial recovery.
- 2025-09-21: added extra logging on embedding worker, observed occasional different embedding_dim values.

Commands/requests I reproduced locally (minimal):
1) curl to hosted embeddings endpoint (anonymized):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-768","input":["foo","bar"]}' | jq .

Observed output (one of the failing responses):
{
  "error": "internal server error",
  "message": "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 768 but got 512"
}

2) Python probe to inspect numpy shapes (local):
--- file: quick_probe.py ---
import requests, numpy as np
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.test/v1/embeddings', json={"model":"open-embed-768","input":["x"]}, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer x'})
print('status', resp.status_code)
try:
    j = resp.json()
    print('keys', j.keys())
    print('shape', np.array(j['data'][0]['embedding']).shape)
except Exception as e:
    print('json err', e, resp.text)
---
When good: status 200, shape (768,)
When bad: status 500, body contains 'embedding_dim mismatch', or occasionally returns embedding length 512 -> shape (512,) which breaks rerank.

Server logs (redacted snippets):
[2025-09-20T10:33:12Z] worker-7 WARN embeddings: model open-embed-768 reported output_dim=512 (expected 768)
[2025-09-20T10:33:12Z] worker-7 ERROR rerank: failed to construct matrix: shapes (N,512) vs (N,768)
[2025-09-20T10:34:45Z] router INFO routing: fallback to compatible-embed-512 for tenant=acme-corp
[2025-09-20T10:36:01Z] infra WARN batching: large-batch delay=3.2s (queue length 24)

Observed patterns / notes:
- Dimension mismatch is not constant; same model id sometimes returns 768 dim and sometimes 512.
- Latency spikes correlate with a period where a portion of traffic was routed to a quantized variant (open-embed-768-4bit) and a separate instance serving open-embed-512.
- Autoscaler bounced some pods around 10:30 — possible during rollout of a node image that included a new model artifact mapping.
- Rerank code is strict about dims (np.dot assumes same last dim). We see re-rank failures bubble up as 500s & slow retries.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model artifact mislabelling: model id "open-embed-768" points to two different artifacts on two pools (one actually produces 512-dim). Likely bad release that updated artifact registry without changing name.
2) Runtime model-quantization compatibility: quantized kernel returns reduced-dim compressed vectors (512) when run with certain kernel selection heuristics.
3) Dynamic model routing bug: routing policy fallback incorrectly maps model id to a different canonical model (compatible-embed-512) under capacity pressure.
4) Memory corruption / packing bug: KV cache or memcopy truncation in the inference pipeline leading to 512-length slices returned.
5) Upstream client changed prompt shape causing model to return different projection head (less likely).

Things I tried (and results):
- Forced model pin to a single worker pool (pinning to pool-A with image v1.4.1): shape stabilized -> 768. Good signal for hypothesis #1.
- Pulled recent artifact manifests on worker nodes and compared checksums between pool-A and pool-B: found mismatched artifact id for the same model tag (open-embed-768 -> artifact-abc123 vs artifact-def456).
- Replayed traffic with header X-Debug-Model: true to force logs: observed worker pool-B reporting model_version: artifact-def456 metadata: {embedding_dim:512}.
- Temporarily updated rerank to do a soft-check (pad/truncate) to avoid 500s for emergency mitigation (PR 278). This prevented 500s but produced poor rerank quality; rolled back after artifact rollback.

Quick reproduction steps for eng-sre:
1) Send 1000 concurrent small embedding requests pinned to model=open-embed-768 across multiple zones.
2) Watch worker logs for message 'reported output_dim=512'.
3) Check /artifacts/manifest on the worker node and compare model tag -> artifact id.

Mitigations applied so far:
- Rollback artifact mapping on pool-B to artifact-abc123 (rev from 2025-09-10) -> decreased mismatch reports dramatically.
- Short-term rerank guard: if embedding length != expected, return 424 to caller (so caller can decide). This was later changed to 503/traceable error in the hosted API to preserve semantics.

Next steps (open):
- Incident postmortem draft: collect all manifests, router routing logs, autoscaler events between 10:00–12:00 UTC. (I will start a Confluence page).
- Strongly recommend adding an artifact->model tag immutability check in deployment pipeline: CI should fail if two pools claim different artifact checksums for same model tag.
- Add model metadata enforcement at serving side: when worker loads model, emit metric gauge model_expected_dim and model_reported_dim and fire an alert if mismatch.
- Add automated integration test in canary rollout that sends a few embedding probes and verifies dimension.
- Consider allowing soft-compatibility (pad/truncate) as opt-in with QA on rerank quality; but default should be strict.

Notes to self (todo):
- Email ops with timeline + suggested CI gating.
- Add Jira updates to JIRA-ML-1428 with artifacts and logs.
- Follow up with infra on autoscaler churn around 10:30 — is that normal for that release window?
- Check if any recent PRs touched model-tagging scripts (deploy/manifest-sync).

Scratch/old commands (kept in case useful):
- grep -R "output_dim" /var/log/redwood/serving/* | sed -n '1,200p'
- kubectl get pods -l app=embeddings -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'
- kubectl exec -it pod/emb-worker-7 -- cat /artifacts/manifest | jq .

Final quick note: root cause looks like an artifact-tag mismatch across pools (human release/manifest-sync mistake). The immediate production fix (rollback on pool-B) removed the bulk of errors. Still need CI + serving-side guard to prevent recurrence.

End of scratchpad.

-- Maya
